note: Retry, timeout and backoff mechanics beyond the core set in 20-retry.json — drafted from the claims the skills actually make, each verified against both sampled SDKs.

assertions.claim: RetryOptions lives in {RootNamespace}.Core.Configuration — the namespace the Customize sample's using directive imports.
OnRetry is an Action<RetryAttempt>? — a synchronous void callback. That is why the sample's `attempt => Console.WriteLine(...)` binds; there is no async form to await.
OnRetry defaults to null — nothing observes a retry until you assign it.
Timeout is nullable — `Timeout = null` is a legal value, not a compile error.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Notes, the `Timeout` is per attempt bullet

assertions.claim: Setting Timeout = null disables the per-attempt timeout entirely — the timeout strategy is added only when Timeout has a value.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Notes, the `Timeout` is per attempt bullet

assertions.claim: Timeout is per attempt, not cumulative: retry is registered before — therefore outside — the timeout strategy, so every attempt gets its own full Timeout.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Notes, the `Timeout` is per attempt bullet; § Bounding a call, three-layers table

assertions.claim: The nth retry waits Delay * BackOffFactor^(n-1): the growth term is Delay multiplied by BackOffFactor raised to the 0-based attempt number, so the first retry waits exactly one Delay.
UseExponentialBackoff = false gives a constant Delay between attempts — the other arm of the same expression is the bare Delay, with no growth term.
The jitter term is random(0, MaxJitter) — a uniform draw scaled by MaxJitter, not a fixed or proportional fudge.
Backoff and jitter are summed and then clamped to the 60s ceiling, so a large BackOffFactor cannot push a single delay past a minute.
Retry-After is honoured in both wire forms — delta-seconds, and an HTTP date turned into a delay by subtracting the current time.
A Retry-After value is clamped at both ends — a date already in the past floors at zero instead of producing a negative delay, and anything above the ceiling becomes 60s.
The 60s delay ceiling is not configurable — it is an internal constant of the pipeline factory and is never exposed as a public member.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Notes, the Retry-After bullet (a hard 60s ceiling that is not configurable)

assertions.claim: Retry eligibility is decided per request type before the pipeline runs: IRequest.CanRetry alone picks between the retrying pipeline and the timeout-only one.

The pipeline goes empty only when retries are off AND Timeout is null — so Disabled() keeps the per-attempt Timeout, and a client with both off still constructs instead of tripping Polly's zero-strategy builder.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Making a write safe under retries (Disabled() keeps the per-attempt Timeout)

assertions.claim: The AttemptNumber on the RetryAttempt handed to OnRetry is 1-based — the first retry reports 1, not Polly's 0.
RetryAttempt.Reason is RetryReason.Failure(Exception) when the attempt threw — the per-attempt timeout included — and RetryReason.Status(HttpStatusCode) when it returned a retryable status.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Notes, the OnRetry Reason bullet; dotnet-testing § Notes

assertions.claim: The RetryAttempt handed to OnRetry carries AttemptNumber, Delay and Reason — the three members the samples read off it.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Retries, the Customize sample; § Notes, the OnRetry Reason bullet

assertions.claim: Exactly three body types are unconditionally retry-eligible — JSON, form-url-encoded and empty-body. With binary pinned to false and multipart conditional, that fixes all five.

The body types the eligibility rule enumerates — binary, multipart, JSON, form-url-encoded, empty — are the complete set of IRequest implementations; there is no sixth kind with unstated retry behaviour.

A TaskCanceledException — from your own CancellationToken, or from HttpClient.Timeout — is not in the retry set and ends the call where it fires: neither cancellation type is named anywhere in the pipeline the factory builds.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Notes, 'Three things trigger a retry'; § Bounding a call

assertions.claim: Nothing in Core reads response.RequestMessage — the verb the predicate filters on comes from the resilience context — so a test stub that leaves RequestMessage unset still exercises retries.
assertions.defends: dotnet-testing § Notes, the stub's response.RequestMessage line
